signals.signal: Board approval and ESMS Policy integrated into Credit/Risk Management
signals.definition: A formally approved environmental and social management system (ESMS) that sets the institution’s risk appetite, responsibilities and minimum controls, and is embedded in credit and other risk-taking decisions.
signals.measurement: Assess current board approval, coverage of material products and sectors, integration into credit policies and delegated authorities, named control owners, and evidence of at least annual effectiveness review.
signals.evidence_required: Board-approved ESMS or E&S policy; board or committee minutes; credit and risk manuals; risk-appetite statement; responsibility matrix; latest ESMS review or assurance report.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of an approved ESMS integrated into credit and risk management. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — An approved policy exists but covers only selected products, entities or decision stages. 3 — The ESMS is embedded in the main credit workflow with defined roles and documented approvals. 4 — All material portfolios are covered, exceptions and performance are monitored, and results reach senior governance forums. 5 — The ESMS is independently tested, demonstrably affects financing decisions, and is improved using trend, incident and portfolio-risk data.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 1; IFC Performance Standard 1
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Core control for identifying and managing E&S risk before financing decisions.

references.label: IFC Environmental and Social Performance Standards

signals.signal: E&S screening and risk classification of transactions
signals.definition: A repeatable process for identifying E&S risks in every in-scope transaction and assigning a risk category that determines the depth of review, approval and monitoring.
signals.measurement: Calculate the number and value of in-scope transactions screened and classified divided by total in-scope transactions; test classification quality, override rates, timeliness and portfolio coverage.
signals.evidence_required: Screening procedure and taxonomy; completed screening checklists; system extracts; transaction samples; risk-category register; exception and override logs; quality-assurance results.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of systematic E&S screening and risk classification. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A documented method is piloted or covers less than 60% of in-scope activity. 3 — The method covers most material activity, normally at least 60%, with recorded risk categories. 4 — Coverage is normally at least 85%, with automated controls, exception reporting and periodic quality review. 5 — Coverage is normally at least 95%; classification quality is independently tested and portfolio trends drive risk appetite and sector action.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 1; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Ensures transactions receive a risk category and proper level of review.

signals.signal: E&S due diligence for high-risk clients/projects
signals.definition: Enhanced E&S due diligence proportionate to the risk of high-risk clients and projects, including assessment of impacts, management capacity, applicable standards and required mitigation.
signals.measurement: Measure the share of high-risk transactions receiving documented enhanced due diligence, site review or specialist input; track action-plan quality, pre-disbursement conditions and unresolved findings.
signals.evidence_required: Enhanced due-diligence procedure; E&S impact assessments; site-visit reports; independent expert reports; client action plans; approval memoranda; conditions-precedent and closure evidence.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of enhanced due diligence for high-risk financing. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A procedure exists but is used inconsistently or after approval rather than before commitment. 3 — Most high-risk transactions receive documented review and material issues are reflected in approval conditions. 4 — All high-risk transactions receive risk-proportionate review, specialist input where needed, and tracked action plans. 5 — Independent testing confirms complete coverage and effective mitigation; serious findings demonstrably lead to redesign, escalation or declined financing.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 1; IFC Performance Standards
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: High-risk exposures create major environmental, social, legal and reputational risks.

references.label: IFC Environmental and Social Performance Standards

signals.signal: Monitoring of E&S conditions, covenants and performance
signals.definition: Ongoing supervision of agreed E&S conditions after approval and disbursement, including covenants, client action plans, incidents and changes in risk profile.
signals.measurement: Track the percentage of relevant facilities with current monitoring, overdue actions, covenant breaches, incident response times and closure rates, segmented by risk category.
signals.evidence_required: Loan covenants; monitoring schedules; client reports; site-monitoring reports; action-plan tracker; breach and waiver logs; escalation records; portfolio monitoring dashboard.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of post-approval monitoring of E&S conditions and performance. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Monitoring requirements are documented for selected transactions but completion is inconsistent. 3 — Material high-risk facilities are monitored on schedule and breaches are logged with owners. 4 — Risk-based monitoring covers all relevant facilities, overdue actions and incidents are escalated, and management receives trend reports. 5 — Monitoring is independently tested, connected to credit review and pricing or limits, and shows timely closure and improving client performance.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 1; IFC Performance Standard 1
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Confirms E&S requirements are followed after approval and disbursement.

references.label: IFC Environmental and Social Performance Standards

signals.signal: Exclusion list, escalation and remediation procedures
signals.definition: A controlled framework defining prohibited activities, escalation thresholds, approval exceptions and corrective action when clients or transactions breach E&S requirements.
signals.measurement: Review exclusion-list currency and scope; count screened matches, exceptions, breaches, remediation plans, repeat breaches, declined transactions and closure time.
signals.evidence_required: Approved exclusion list; escalation matrix; exception policy; screening logs; committee decisions; breach register; remediation plans; termination or decline records; periodic control testing.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of an effective exclusion, escalation and remediation framework. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — An exclusion list exists but is incomplete, outdated or weakly connected to origination systems. 3 — The list and escalation rules are approved and applied to the main financing processes; breaches are recorded. 4 — Automated or mandatory controls cover all material activities, exceptions require senior approval, and remediation is tracked to closure. 5 — Independent testing confirms effectiveness; repeat breaches are rare and evidence shows that prohibited or unremediated exposures are declined, exited or restricted.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 1; IFC Sustainability Framework
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Prevents prohibited activities and provides a process for breaches.

references.label: IFC Environmental and Social Performance Standards

signals.signal: Application of NSBP sector guidelines to relevant power, agriculture, and oil & gas exposures
signals.definition: Application of the CBN’s sector-specific sustainable-banking requirements to financing in power, agriculture, and oil and gas where the institution has relevant exposure.
signals.measurement: For each relevant sector, measure the number and value of transactions assessed with the applicable sector guideline divided by total relevant transactions; review required metrics, mitigants and reporting completeness. Use N/A only where there is demonstrably no relevant exposure.
signals.evidence_required: Sector exposure report; CBN sector checklists or equivalent procedures; completed transaction assessments; sector approval templates; risk and impact KPIs; regulatory returns; exception records.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of the applicable CBN sector guidelines. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — One or more relevant sector procedures exist but are incomplete or applied to a limited sample. 3 — Sector requirements are used for most material exposures and required transaction data is retained. 4 — All relevant exposures are assessed, monitored and reported using sector-specific controls and KPIs. 5 — Independent review confirms complete application and evidence shows sector data shaping limits, client engagement, product design and portfolio transition.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP sector guidelines and reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Important for high-impact sectors but applies only where the institution has relevant sector exposure.

signals.signal: Environmental management programme with measured energy, water, waste and GHG data, and a trend
signals.definition: An operational environmental management programme covering energy, greenhouse-gas emissions, water, materials and waste across the institution’s facilities, with quantified performance trends.
signals.measurement: Measure reporting-boundary coverage; Scope 1 and 2 emissions; energy and water use; waste generated, diverted and disposed; intensity indicators; and at least two years of comparable trend data.
signals.evidence_required: Environmental policy and programme; facility data; utility and fuel records; GHG inventory and methodology; waste records; boundary and base-year statement; dashboards; internal review or assurance.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of a measured environmental management programme. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A baseline or selected environmental data exists for limited sites or indicators. 3 — A formal programme covers major sites and reports energy, water, waste and GHG data for the current period. 4 — Coverage is enterprise-wide, targets and intensity metrics are monitored, and comparable multi-year trends demonstrate control. 5 — Data is externally assured or independently verified, material reductions are achieved against science- or policy-aligned targets, and findings guide investment decisions.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 2; GHG Protocol
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Highest because it provides measurable, comparable and trend-based evidence of the institution's operational footprint.

signals.signal: Community investment aligned to national development priorities, with outcomes reported
signals.definition: Community investment that is aligned with identified Nigerian development needs and managed for measurable outcomes rather than reported only as expenditure or activity.
signals.measurement: Track investment by theme and geography, beneficiaries reached, outcome indicators, partner performance, additionality, beneficiary feedback and progress against programme targets.
signals.evidence_required: Community-investment strategy; needs assessments; approved budgets; partner agreements; beneficiary data; outcome evaluations; feedback records; impact reports; governance approvals.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of outcome-led community investment. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Programmes and expenditure are documented but needs, targets or outcomes are unclear. 3 — Material programmes align to stated development priorities and report beneficiaries and basic results. 4 — A portfolio framework sets outcome targets, evaluates partners, captures beneficiary feedback and reports results by theme and location. 5 — Independent evaluation demonstrates sustained outcomes and additionality; lessons transparently change programme design and capital allocation.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 2
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Kept moderate because spending on community projects can be highly visible without necessarily producing measurable outcomes.

signals.signal: Labour, workplace and occupational health & safety standards
signals.definition: Policies and controls that provide fair labour practices, safe and healthy work, equal opportunity and effective workforce protections for employees and relevant contracted workers.
signals.measurement: Assess workforce and contractor coverage; fatalities, recordable injuries and lost-time rates; training; hazard closure; grievances; discrimination cases; turnover and compliance with labour requirements.
signals.evidence_required: HR and OHS policies; risk assessments; incident registers; training records; worker grievance logs; workforce and contractor statistics; inspections; corrective-action reports; audit or certification records.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of effective labour and occupational health and safety standards. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Policies exist but coverage, incident data or worker remedies are incomplete. 3 — Core labour and OHS controls operate for employees, material incidents are logged, and required training is delivered. 4 — Controls cover employees and relevant contractors, leading indicators and grievances are monitored, and corrective actions close on time. 5 — Independent assurance shows mature prevention, strong worker participation, transparent incident learning and sustained improvement in material workforce outcomes.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 2; IFC Performance Standard 2
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: The institution directly controls employee working conditions and carries material legal and social responsibility.

references.label: IFC Environmental and Social Performance Standards

signals.signal: Environmental targets across branches/offices
signals.definition: Specific, measurable and time-bound environmental performance targets cascaded across material branches, offices, data centres and other controlled facilities.
signals.measurement: Measure the percentage of material sites covered by targets, target quality, baseline and deadline completeness, performance against trajectory, corrective actions and management review frequency.
signals.evidence_required: Approved targets; facility-level action plans; site registers; baseline calculations; performance dashboards; energy or water projects; variance analysis; management review minutes.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of environmental targets across the operational estate. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Targets are aspirational, lack baselines or apply to only a few sites. 3 — Quantified targets and action plans cover major facilities, with periodic progress data. 4 — Time-bound targets cover all material facilities, have accountable owners and trigger corrective action when off track. 5 — Targets are externally validated or benchmarked, progress is independently verified, and the institution demonstrates sustained absolute and intensity improvement.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 2; NGX disclosure guidance
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Targets make performance trackable across the institution.

signals.signal: Sustainable procurement and supplier standards
signals.definition: Integration of environmental, labour, human-rights, ethics and inclusion requirements into supplier selection, contracting, monitoring and remediation.
signals.measurement: Track spend and supplier coverage of E&S screening and contractual clauses, high-risk supplier due diligence, audit findings, corrective-action closure, repeat non-compliance and exits.
signals.evidence_required: Supplier code; procurement policy; pre-qualification questionnaire; standard clauses; supplier risk segmentation; assessments and audits; corrective-action tracker; termination records; spend analysis.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of sustainable procurement and supplier standards. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A supplier code or isolated screening exists but is not embedded in procurement decisions. 3 — Minimum E&S clauses and screening apply to material new suppliers, with some monitoring. 4 — Risk-based due diligence covers material spend and existing suppliers; findings and remediation are tracked. 5 — Supplier performance affects award and renewal decisions, high-risk supply chains are independently reviewed, and outcome data demonstrates sustained improvement.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 2; IFC Performance Standard 2
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Extends environmental responsibility to vendors and suppliers.

references.label: IFC Environmental and Social Performance Standards

signals.signal: Renewable energy and energy-efficiency initiatives
signals.definition: Implementation of renewable-energy and energy-efficiency measures that reduce fossil-fuel dependence, energy cost and operational emissions.
signals.measurement: Measure renewable share of electricity, renewable capacity installed, energy use and intensity, generator fuel avoided, verified savings, emissions avoided, site coverage and return on investment.
signals.evidence_required: Energy audits; project business cases; installation and purchase records; renewable-energy contracts; metered consumption; fuel logs; savings calculations; verification reports; target dashboards.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of renewable-energy and energy-efficiency action. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Energy audits, pilots or isolated installations exist without material measured savings. 3 — Projects cover important sites and report energy or emissions savings against a baseline. 4 — A funded portfolio programme covers most material facilities and demonstrates recurring savings and growing renewable share. 5 — Independent verification shows substantial sustained reductions, ambitious forward targets and systematic reinvestment based on marginal cost and carbon impact.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 2; GHG Protocol
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Elevated — direct renewable-energy market signal for Nigeria.

signals.signal: Human rights, labour and non-discrimination policy
signals.definition: A senior-approved commitment to respect internationally recognised human and labour rights, prevent discrimination and apply the commitment across operations and business relationships.
signals.measurement: Assess approval level, rights and stakeholder groups covered, application to employees, clients and suppliers, communication, review frequency, ownership and consistency with Nigerian law and the UN Guiding Principles.
signals.evidence_required: Human-rights or responsible-business policy; code of conduct; board approval; HR and supplier policies; public commitments; communication records; policy review; responsibility matrix.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of a comprehensive human-rights and non-discrimination policy. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A public commitment or code exists but has narrow coverage or unclear accountability. 3 — A senior-approved policy covers operations and material business relationships and is communicated internally. 4 — The policy is embedded in procedures, contracts, training and governance, with periodic review and public disclosure. 5 — Independent review confirms alignment with international standards and evidence shows the policy preventing harm and shaping decisions across the value chain.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 3; UN Guiding Principles
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Establishes the minimum standards for employees, customers, and communities that the institution commits to adoption to be followed by implemented

references.label: UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights

signals.signal: Human rights due diligence embedded in client and transaction assessment
signals.definition: A process for identifying, preventing, mitigating and accounting for human-rights impacts in clients, transactions, suppliers and the institution’s own operations.
signals.measurement: Measure the number and value of in-scope transactions and high-risk suppliers assessed; issues identified; mitigations placed in contracts; escalations, declines and follow-up completion.
signals.evidence_required: Human-rights due-diligence procedure and tools; transaction and supplier samples; impact assessments; approval records; contractual mitigants; escalation and decline logs; monitoring reports.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of human-rights due diligence in decisions. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Risk questions exist but are used inconsistently or without documented follow-up. 3 — A documented process covers selected high-risk clients, transactions or suppliers and records mitigations. 4 — Risk-based due diligence covers all material relationships, is completed before commitment and feeds approval and monitoring. 5 — Independent testing confirms effectiveness; affected stakeholders inform assessments and evidence shows prevention, mitigation, decline and remediation decisions.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 3; UN Guiding Principles
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Reduces risk of financing activities linked to social harm.

references.label: UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights
IFC Environmental and Social Performance Standards

signals.signal: Awareness, capacity building and training for stakeholders
signals.definition: Role-appropriate education that enables employees, clients, suppliers and other relevant stakeholders to understand human-rights risks, responsibilities and escalation routes.
signals.measurement: Track priority populations, training coverage, completion, assessment results, refresher frequency, role-specific content, participant feedback and changes in behaviour or control performance.
signals.evidence_required: Training-needs assessment; curricula; attendance and completion records; assessments; communication materials; stakeholder workshops; feedback; effectiveness evaluation; remediation for non-completion.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of effective human-rights awareness and capability. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — General awareness is delivered to a limited audience without role-specific learning or effectiveness checks. 3 — Priority employees receive recurring role-based training and completion is tracked. 4 — Employees and relevant external stakeholders are covered according to risk; knowledge and behaviour are assessed and gaps remediated. 5 — Independent or outcome-based evaluation demonstrates sustained capability, improved decisions and proactive knowledge-sharing with clients, suppliers and peers.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principles 3 and 7; UN Guiding Principles
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Create Stakeholder awareness and support prevention of Human Right Violations

references.label: UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights

signals.signal: Accessible grievance mechanism with cases logged, tracked and resolved
signals.definition: Trusted channels through which workers, customers and affected communities can raise human-rights concerns and receive timely, fair and rights-compatible resolution without retaliation.
signals.measurement: Assess channel accessibility and stakeholder coverage; cases by type; acknowledgement and resolution time; overdue cases; satisfaction, recurrence, retaliation controls and remedy provided.
signals.evidence_required: Grievance procedure; channel descriptions; case register; service standards; anonymised case files; remedy and closure evidence; stakeholder communication; trend analysis; governance reports.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of an accessible and effective human-rights grievance mechanism. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A generic complaints channel exists but accessibility, confidentiality, rights expertise or case tracking is weak. 3 — Defined channels and service standards cover key stakeholder groups and cases are logged to closure. 4 — Multiple accessible channels, anti-retaliation controls, escalation and trend reporting operate across workers, customers and affected communities. 5 — The mechanism meets recognised effectiveness criteria, is designed with users, independently reviewed and demonstrably provides remedy and prevents recurrence.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 3; UN Guiding Principles; IFC Performance Standard 1
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Gives employees, customers and affected communities a practical route to report harm and seek remedy.

references.label: UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights
IFC Environmental and Social Performance Standards

signals.signal: Tracking and remediation of human-rights incidents
signals.definition: Systematic identification, investigation, remediation and learning from actual or potential human-rights incidents connected to the institution’s operations, financing or business relationships.
signals.measurement: Track incidents and substantiated cases by severity and relationship; investigation time; remedies; overdue actions; recurrence; affected people engaged; and disclosure of material incidents.
signals.evidence_required: Incident taxonomy and register; investigation files; root-cause analysis; remediation plans; affected-party engagement; closure approvals; trend reports; board escalation; public disclosures where material.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of human-rights incident tracking and remediation. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Incidents are handled case by case without a complete register, severity rules or remedy tracking. 3 — A formal process logs and investigates material incidents and assigns corrective actions. 4 — All relevant incidents are severity-rated, escalated, remediated and analysed for recurring causes, with governance reporting. 5 — Independent review and stakeholder feedback confirm effective remedy; transparent learning produces demonstrable policy, control and client-engagement improvements.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 3; UN Guiding Principles
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Shows whether issues are corrected and monitored over time.

references.label: UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights

signals.signal: Financial products/credit specifically targeting women
signals.definition: Financial products, credit facilities or delivery propositions intentionally designed around the needs and constraints of women and women-owned enterprises.
signals.measurement: Assess the number and range of active propositions, eligible customers reached, applications, approvals, active usage, portfolio quality and customer outcomes, disaggregated by product and customer segment.
signals.evidence_required: Product papers and eligibility rules; gender-market research; approval minutes; marketing and delivery materials; customer and portfolio extracts; usage and outcome analysis; customer feedback; periodic product reviews.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of financial products or credit specifically targeting women. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — One pilot or relabelled mainstream product exists with little evidence of customer research or uptake. 3 — At least one approved proposition addresses documented barriers and reports reach and portfolio performance. 4 — A coordinated product range uses gender-disaggregated research, has targets and reports active use, quality and customer outcomes. 5 — Women co-design propositions; results show sustained scale, responsible portfolio performance and demonstrable economic outcomes, with continuous improvement based on data.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 4; CBN financial-inclusion strategy
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Directly expands women's access to financial services.

signals.signal: Percentage/value of financing to women-owned businesses
signals.definition: The institution's financing exposure and flow to businesses that meet a documented, consistently applied definition of women-owned or women-led.
signals.measurement: Report customer count, approvals, new disbursements and outstanding value to women-owned businesses as percentages of the relevant business or MSME totals, with period-on-period growth, portfolio quality and reconciled data lineage.
signals.evidence_required: Approved women-owned-business definition; customer-identification fields; loan and disbursement extracts; denominator reconciliation; management dashboards; portfolio-quality reports; data-quality testing.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of measured financing to women-owned businesses. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Anecdotal values or customer counts are reported without a stable definition, denominator or reconciliation. 3 — A documented definition supports periodic count or value reporting for a material portfolio. 4 — Count and value shares, flows, growth and portfolio quality are reported with defined boundaries and data controls. 5 — Independently validated data demonstrates sustained responsible growth and material market reach, and informs targets, product design and capital allocation.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 4; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Provides measurable evidence of actual economic support.

signals.signal: Women represented in workforce, management, leadership against the 40% NSBP benchmark
signals.definition: Representation of women across the total workforce, management, senior leadership and board, assessed against the NSBP's historical 40% benchmark and the institution's own approved targets.
signals.measurement: Calculate women as a percentage of each defined workforce level using consistent headcount denominators; report hiring, promotion, succession, turnover and year-on-year movement, and explain target gaps.
signals.evidence_required: HR system extracts and organisation structure; level definitions; board and committee composition; recruitment, promotion and attrition data; succession plans; target dashboards; data reconciliation.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of women's representation across workforce and leadership. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Representation is known for the total workforce only or remains materially below targets with no credible plan. 3 — Reliable data covers workforce and management, with approved actions addressing material gaps. 4 — Representation and talent-flow data cover all levels, progress is reviewed by leadership and the 40% benchmark is met in significant decision-making tiers. 5 — Balanced representation is sustained across material levels and pipelines, supported by independently validated data and demonstrably equitable hiring, promotion and retention outcomes.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 4; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Measures internal gender inclusion and advancement opportunities.

signals.signal: Internal measurable gender targets
signals.definition: Approved gender-equity objectives expressed through measurable baselines, targets, accountable owners and deadlines for customer and workforce outcomes.
signals.measurement: Assess target coverage, baseline and methodology quality, due dates, responsible owners, progress against trajectory, variance explanations and corrective action.
signals.evidence_required: Approved targets and baselines; gender strategy; scorecards; owner assignments; periodic performance reports; variance analysis; corrective-action records; governance minutes.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of measurable gender targets. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A public ambition exists but lacks a baseline, deadline, owner or complete measure. 3 — Quantified targets cover at least one material customer and one workforce outcome and are periodically tracked. 4 — Time-bound targets cover all material gender outcomes, are cascaded to accountable leaders and trigger corrective action. 5 — Ambitious targets are transparently reported and independently validated, with sustained delivery and target renewal based on outcome and intersectional analysis.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 4; GRI 2
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Enables monitoring of gaps and progress over time.

signals.signal: Policy, oversight committee, pipeline development, mentoring and retention of female talent
signals.definition: A coherent governance and talent system that assigns oversight for gender equity and builds, advances and retains female talent through policy, succession, sponsorship, mentoring and inclusive work practices.
signals.measurement: Assess policy and committee authority, meeting frequency, succession-pipeline depth, programme coverage, promotion and retention rates, return after parental leave, and action taken on adverse trends.
signals.evidence_required: Gender or diversity policy; committee charter and minutes; succession and talent reviews; mentoring or sponsorship records; promotion, retention and parental-leave data; action plans; employee feedback.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of gender governance, pipeline development and retention. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Isolated mentoring or diversity activities exist without accountable oversight or outcome tracking. 3 — An approved policy, named oversight forum and recurring talent programmes cover priority employee groups. 4 — Governance reviews disaggregated pipeline, promotion and retention outcomes and directs action on gaps across all levels. 5 — Evidence shows sustained equitable progression and retention; programme effectiveness is independently evaluated and employee insight continuously shapes policy and investment.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 4; GRI 2
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Creates the institutional structure needed to sustain female representation and advancement over time.

signals.signal: Pay equity review and workplace protections, including anti-harassment machinery
signals.definition: Controls that identify and remediate gender-related pay inequity and protect workers from harassment, discrimination and retaliation through trusted prevention, reporting and remedy mechanisms.
signals.measurement: Assess pay-equity review scope and methodology, adjusted gaps and remediation; policy and training coverage; reported cases, acknowledgement and resolution time, recurrence, retaliation controls and employee confidence.
signals.evidence_required: Pay-equity analysis; remuneration and job-level data; remediation approvals; anti-harassment policy; training records; confidential case register; investigation and remedy files; culture surveys; board reports.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of pay equity and effective workplace protections. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Policies exist but pay gaps are not analysed or complaints controls are informal and weakly evidenced. 3 — Periodic pay review and formal anti-harassment channels cover employees, with cases tracked to closure. 4 — Adjusted pay analysis covers material employee groups, unjustified gaps are remediated and prevention, investigation and anti-retaliation controls are monitored. 5 — Independent review confirms equitable pay and trusted rights-compatible remedies, with transparent trend learning and sustained improvement in employee experience.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principles 3 and 4; IFC Performance Standard 2

signals.justification: Important for workplace equality but often less consistently disclosed or measurable across institutions.

signals.signal: Growth in underserved/unbanked customers served
signals.definition: Sustained growth in previously unbanked or underserved people and enterprises who actively use appropriate regulated financial services.
signals.measurement: Measure verified new-to-formal-finance customers, active customers and usage frequency by priority demographic, geography and enterprise type; report dormancy, retention and outcome indicators rather than account openings alone.
signals.evidence_required: Customer classification rules; KYC and account data; active-use methodology; customer and transaction extracts; geographic and demographic breakdowns; retention analysis; impact or customer research.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of growth in actively served underserved or unbanked customers. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Account-opening activity is reported without reliable underserved classification or active-use evidence. 3 — A documented methodology identifies priority customers and reports reach and some active-use data. 4 — Targets and disaggregated data demonstrate sustained growth, usage and retention across priority segments, with product action on gaps. 5 — Independently validated data demonstrates material additional reach and sustained beneficial use, with customer outcomes shaping strategy and resource allocation.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 5; CBN financial-inclusion strategy
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Directly measures contribution to expanding access to finance.

signals.signal: Channel accessibility: agent banking, digital channels and accessibility for persons with disabilities
signals.definition: Reliable physical and digital service channels that are geographically accessible, affordable, safe and usable by priority groups, including persons with disabilities.
signals.measurement: Measure active agents and service points, underserved-area coverage, uptime, transaction success, digital active use, cash availability, accessibility conformance, assisted-service availability, fraud and complaint rates.
signals.evidence_required: Agent and branch registers; geospatial coverage; uptime and transaction logs; channel accessibility assessment; disability-access features; agent liquidity reports; fraud and complaint analysis; remediation plans.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of accessible agent, digital and disability-inclusive channels. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Channels exist but coverage, reliability or disability accessibility is not systematically assessed. 3 — Material channels have basic reach, uptime and accessibility measures and identified gaps are assigned. 4 — Data demonstrates reliable multi-channel access across priority locations and user groups, with controls for safety, liquidity and service quality. 5 — Inclusive design and independent accessibility testing produce sustained high reliability and demonstrable access gains for underserved and disabled customers.
signals.primary_framework: CBN financial-inclusion strategy; CBN NSBP Principle 5
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Critical infrastructure for access, but weighted below actual reach to avoid double-counting the same inclusion outcome.

signals.signal: Affordable products for low-income groups/MSMEs
signals.definition: Products for low-income customers and MSMEs whose total cost, terms, entry requirements and delivery model are appropriate and do not create avoidable hardship.
signals.measurement: Compare fees, effective rates, minimum balances, collateral and transaction costs with mainstream alternatives and customer income or cash-flow patterns; track uptake, repeat use, delinquency, restructuring and customer outcomes.
signals.evidence_required: Product and pricing papers; total-cost calculations; affordability or suitability tests; customer research; portfolio and usage data; arrears and restructuring reports; complaints; periodic product reviews.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of affordable products for low-income customers and MSMEs. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A low-cost label is used without total-cost, suitability or customer-outcome analysis. 3 — Approved products address documented affordability barriers and report uptake and portfolio quality. 4 — Total cost and suitability are routinely tested, targets cover priority segments and adverse customer outcomes trigger redesign or remediation. 5 — Transparent, independently evaluated propositions deliver sustained responsible access and beneficial outcomes at scale without hidden cost or exclusionary conditions.
signals.primary_framework: CBN financial-inclusion strategy; CBN NSBP Principle 5
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Shows products are genuinely accessible, not merely available.

signals.signal: Inclusion performance tracked by gender/location/type
signals.definition: A reliable inclusion data system that disaggregates customer reach, usage, service quality and outcomes by gender, location, customer or enterprise type and other material priority characteristics.
signals.measurement: Assess field coverage and completeness, data definitions, consent and privacy controls, reconciliation, error rates, reporting frequency, trend analysis and documented use in product, channel and risk decisions.
signals.evidence_required: Data dictionary; system-field catalogue; privacy and consent controls; demographic and geographic extracts; quality reports; dashboards; management minutes; decisions or product changes linked to findings.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of disaggregated financial-inclusion performance tracking. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Some demographic data is collected but completeness, definitions or use are weak. 3 — Core reach and usage indicators are regularly split by gender, location and customer type with basic quality controls. 4 — Validated disaggregated data covers reach, active use, service and outcomes and routinely informs targets and management action. 5 — Granular, privacy-respecting data is independently tested and demonstrably improves allocation, product design and outcomes for intersecting underserved groups.
signals.primary_framework: CBN financial-inclusion strategy; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Provides evidence that inclusion outcomes are managed.

signals.signal: Financial literacy and consumer-protection initiatives including complaint-resolution performance
signals.definition: Education, fair-treatment and complaint-resolution arrangements that enable customers—especially vulnerable groups—to make informed choices, use services safely and obtain timely remedy.
signals.measurement: Track priority audiences reached and learning outcomes; plain-language and suitability controls; complaints per customer, acknowledgement and resolution within service levels, upheld cases, redress, recurrence, fraud and customer satisfaction.
signals.evidence_required: Consumer-protection policy; literacy strategy and content; attendance and learning assessments; product disclosures; suitability reviews; complaint register and service-level reports; remedy evidence; trend and root-cause analysis.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of financial literacy and effective consumer protection. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — One-off awareness events or a generic complaints desk exist without outcome or resolution-performance data. 3 — Recurring targeted education and formal complaint standards operate, with reach and closure data reported. 4 — Learning and complaint outcomes are disaggregated, service levels and redress are monitored, and root causes drive product and control changes. 5 — Independent evaluation shows sustained capability and fair-treatment outcomes, trusted remedy, low recurrence and proactive protection of vulnerable customers across channels.
signals.primary_framework: CBN financial-inclusion strategy; CBN NSBP Principle 5
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Supports sustainable inclusion but less direct than actual access.

signals.signal: Board-level oversight of sustainability/E&S matters
signals.definition: Explicit board or delegated board-committee accountability for sustainability and E&S matters, supported by sufficient information, expertise and documented challenge.
signals.measurement: Assess mandate, meeting frequency, attendance, agenda coverage, quality of management information, decisions and challenges, action closure, escalation of incidents and annual oversight effectiveness.
signals.evidence_required: Board and committee charters; skills matrix; agendas and minutes; sustainability dashboards; decision and action logs; incident escalations; board evaluations; approved reports and policies.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of effective board-level sustainability oversight. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — The board receives occasional updates but its mandate, information or decisions are unclear. 3 — A board or committee mandate exists and material performance, risks and policies are reviewed at least periodically. 4 — The board regularly challenges strategy, risk appetite, targets and incidents, tracks decisions and has relevant competence. 5 — Independent evaluation demonstrates informed, consequential oversight that shapes capital, risk and remuneration and drives sustained performance improvement.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 6; IFRS S1 governance
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Creates senior accountability and visibility for sustainability issues.

signals.signal: Dedicated sustainability/ESG unit with clear accountability
signals.definition: A dedicated sustainability or ESG function with defined authority, competent staffing, resources and reporting lines sufficient to coordinate implementation across the institution.
signals.measurement: Assess mandate, organisational position, full-time-equivalent staffing, role competence, budget, business-unit responsibilities, escalation rights, performance objectives and delivery against work plans.
signals.evidence_required: Organisation chart; unit charter; job descriptions; staffing and skills records; approved budget; work plan; responsibility matrix; performance reports; escalation and committee records.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of a capable and accountable sustainability function. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Responsibility is informal, part-time or fragmented with limited authority and resources. 3 — A named function and accountable lead have approved roles, resources and a recurring work plan. 4 — The function has sufficient specialists, budget and senior access, coordinates embedded business owners and reports delivery and gaps. 5 — The operating model is independently benchmarked, has strong succession and specialist depth, and demonstrably accelerates institution-wide decisions and outcomes.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 6; IFRS S1 governance
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Assigns responsibility for implementing NSBP requirements.

signals.signal: Approved sustainability policies, strategy and targets
signals.definition: A current, approved and internally coherent set of sustainability policies, strategy, objectives and targets covering the institution's material impacts, risks and opportunities.
signals.measurement: Assess material-topic and entity coverage, approval and review dates, baselines, time-bound targets, accountable owners, resourcing, implementation plans, progress reviews and alignment with business planning.
signals.evidence_required: Strategy and policy suite; materiality assessment; board approvals; targets and baselines; implementation roadmap; budgets; business plans; performance dashboards; annual review and update records.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of approved sustainability policies, strategy and targets. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Documents are fragmented, outdated or mainly aspirational and lack accountable delivery plans. 3 — A current approved strategy and core policies identify material priorities, owners and selected measurable targets. 4 — The strategy covers all material activities, is integrated with planning and budget, and performance against time-bound targets is governed. 5 — Forward-looking strategy, scenarios and independently validated targets demonstrably influence business mix and deliver sustained material outcomes.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 6; IFRS S1 strategy
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Turns commitments into formal expectations and objectives.

signals.signal: ESG integrated into enterprise risk and management decisions
signals.definition: Integration of material sustainability and E&S risks and opportunities into enterprise risk management, risk appetite, planning, product, portfolio and capital decisions.
signals.measurement: Assess risk taxonomy and appetite coverage, ownership, risk assessment and monitoring, scenarios or stress tests, limit and early-warning indicators, decision records, aggregation and linkage to strategy and capital.
signals.evidence_required: ERM framework; risk taxonomy and appetite; risk register; limits and indicators; scenario or stress-test results; portfolio analysis; committee papers; product and capital-allocation decisions; remediation plans.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of ESG integration into enterprise risk and management decisions. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Material issues are discussed separately from ERM and rarely affect limits or decisions. 3 — Selected E&S risks appear in the risk taxonomy and register and are periodically reported. 4 — Material risks and opportunities have appetite metrics, owners, monitoring and scenarios and affect portfolio, product and planning decisions. 5 — Integrated forward-looking risk intelligence, stress testing and outcome data demonstrably shape capital and strategy and are independently challenged.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principles 1 and 6; IFRS S1 risk management
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Shows sustainability is part of core management, not a side activity.

signals.signal: Internal audit/compliance review of E&S implementation
signals.definition: Independent internal-audit and compliance review of whether E&S governance, policies, regulatory obligations and operational controls are designed and operating effectively.
signals.measurement: Assess risk-assessment coverage, audit frequency and scope, control testing, issue severity, overdue findings, repeat findings, compliance monitoring, reporting independence and closure validation.
signals.evidence_required: Audit universe and risk assessment; approved audit plan; audit and compliance reports; working papers or samples; findings tracker; management responses; closure validation; audit-committee minutes.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of independent audit and compliance review of E&S implementation. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Reviews are ad hoc, advisory or limited to document presence without operating-effectiveness testing. 3 — E&S is included in the assurance plan and core controls or obligations are periodically tested. 4 — Risk-based audit and compliance coverage spans all material processes, findings are severity-rated and closure is independently validated. 5 — Coordinated assurance, data analytics and external benchmarking provide reliable board insight, with low repeat findings and evidence of sustained control improvement.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 6; IFRS S1 governance and controls
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Provides internal assurance that requirements are followed.

signals.signal: Linkage of E&S outcomes to remuneration and performance incentives
signals.definition: A transparent link between material sustainability outcomes and performance evaluation or variable remuneration for accountable executives and employees.
signals.measurement: Assess the proportion of relevant roles with specific E&S KPIs, KPI materiality and weighting, target calibration, actual performance and payout adjustment, cascade, malus or clawback and remuneration-governance review.
signals.evidence_required: Remuneration and performance policies; role scorecards; KPI definitions and targets; performance outcomes; award calculations; remuneration-committee papers; malus or clawback provisions; disclosure.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of linkage of E&S outcomes to remuneration and incentives. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A broad sustainability behaviour is mentioned in appraisals but has no measurable effect on awards. 3 — Measurable E&S KPIs apply to selected accountable executives or teams and performance is documented. 4 — Material outcome KPIs with meaningful weight cascade across relevant leaders and demonstrably adjust awards under independent remuneration oversight. 5 — Balanced, externally benchmarked incentives include long-term outcomes and safeguards against misconduct, and evidence shows they drive sustained strategy delivery.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 6; GRI 2 governance disclosures
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Strong evidence of integration but still relatively uncommon and potentially gameable, so it receives a controlled weight.

signals.signal: Board and senior-management sustainability training
signals.definition: Recurring, role-appropriate sustainability education that equips board members and senior management to oversee material impacts, risks, opportunities and reporting obligations.
signals.measurement: Track induction and refresher coverage, attendance, hours, subject relevance, facilitator competence, knowledge assessment, skills gaps and evidence that learning improves challenge or decisions.
signals.evidence_required: Board skills assessment; annual learning plan; curricula and materials; attendance; assessment results; facilitator profiles; evaluations; minutes showing application; gap-remediation plans.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of effective sustainability training for the board and senior management. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — One-off awareness sessions occur without a needs assessment, recurring plan or effectiveness test. 3 — Priority leaders receive recurring role-based training and completion is tracked. 4 — Training responds to assessed skills gaps, covers all relevant leaders and tests knowledge and application in governance decisions. 5 — Independent evaluation shows sustained board competence and consequential challenge, supported by advanced learning, succession planning and external engagement.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 7; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Leadership needs knowledge to provide effective ESG oversight.

signals.signal: E&S training for credit, risk and relevant employees
signals.definition: Practical E&S training for credit, risk, compliance, procurement, operations and other employees whose decisions implement sustainable-banking controls.
signals.measurement: Assess role mapping, priority-population coverage, completion, assessment pass rates, refresher timing, case-based content, observed control quality and remediation for non-completion or weak competence.
signals.evidence_required: Training-needs and role map; annual plan; curricula and case studies; learning-system records; assessments; attendance; quality-review results; post-training control metrics; remediation records.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of effective E&S training for credit, risk and relevant employees. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Generic awareness reaches a limited audience and is not connected to job controls. 3 — Recurring role-based training covers priority teams and completion and basic understanding are tracked. 4 — All in-scope roles receive risk-based learning, competence is tested and control-quality data informs refresher and coaching action. 5 — Outcome evaluation demonstrates sustained expert capability and better decisions, supported by certification, communities of practice and continuous curriculum improvement.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 7; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Frontline staff need practical knowledge to apply E&S controls.

signals.signal: Sustainability training for clients/service providers
signals.definition: Targeted sustainability capacity building for clients, suppliers and service providers whose practices materially affect financed or operational E&S outcomes.
signals.measurement: Track risk-based audience selection, organisations and participants reached, content relevance, completion, knowledge or practice change, follow-up support and resulting risk or performance improvement.
signals.evidence_required: Needs assessment; participant selection; curricula; attendance; pre- and post-assessments; advisory materials; participant feedback; follow-up records; client or supplier improvement plans and outcome evidence.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of effective sustainability training for clients and service providers. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Occasional seminars occur without risk-based targeting, follow-up or outcome evidence. 3 — Recurring training reaches selected high-priority clients or providers and participation and feedback are tracked. 4 — Programmes are tailored by sector and risk, combine learning with follow-up support and demonstrate practice or control improvement. 5 — Partnership-based programmes operate at material scale and independent outcome evaluation shows sustained capability, risk reduction and knowledge replication.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principles 7 and 8; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Extends good practice beyond the institution.

signals.signal: Dedicated specialist resourcing, a ring-fenced budget and assessment of training effectiveness
signals.definition: Sufficient specialist people and ring-fenced financial resources to deliver the capacity-building programme, coupled with systematic evaluation of learning effectiveness.
signals.measurement: Assess specialist capacity and credentials, succession and external support, approved budget versus spend, programme delivery, learner coverage and competency gain, control improvement and return on learning investment.
signals.evidence_required: Resource and skills plan; specialist CVs or certifications; succession plan; approved budget and actual spend; programme calendar; learning analytics; competency and effectiveness reviews; management action.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of specialist resourcing, dedicated budget and training-effectiveness assessment. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Delivery depends on isolated individuals or discretionary funds and effectiveness is inferred from attendance. 3 — Named specialists and an approved budget support recurring programmes, with participant feedback and knowledge tests. 4 — Capacity and spend align to risk and plan; outcome measures connect learning to competence and control performance and drive programme changes. 5 — A resilient expert operating model and independently evaluated learning portfolio demonstrate sustained institution-wide capability and measurable performance return.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 7; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Ensures sustainability capability is permanent rather than dependent on occasional training or individual staff members, Improves quality of assessment/implementation.

signals.signal: Active participation in banking/industry ESG initiatives
signals.definition: Active, sustained participation in credible banking or industry initiatives that advance sustainable-banking standards, implementation or market capability.
signals.measurement: Assess strategic relevance, membership status, attendance, leadership roles, technical contributions, commitments delivered, knowledge transferred internally and identifiable initiative outcomes.
signals.evidence_required: Membership confirmations; initiative terms; attendance; working-group records; authored submissions or tools; commitments and progress reports; internal dissemination; outcome evidence.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of active participation in industry ESG initiatives. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Memberships are listed but contribution, attendance or internal value is not evidenced. 3 — Representatives regularly participate in relevant initiatives and share outputs internally. 4 — The institution leads or makes substantive technical contributions, delivers commitments and applies collective learning to operations. 5 — Recognised leadership produces durable sector standards or market infrastructure and demonstrable shared outcomes beyond the institution.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 8; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Demonstrates engagement with sector sustainability standards.

signals.signal: Partnerships with regulators/development institutions/NGOs
signals.definition: Structured partnerships with regulators, development institutions, civil-society organisations or technical bodies to address priority sustainable-finance or inclusion challenges.
signals.measurement: Assess partner fit, documented objectives, governance, resources, beneficiary or market reach, milestones, risks, evaluation and outcomes relative to the partnership's baseline.
signals.evidence_required: Partnership agreements; theory of change or work plan; governance minutes; budgets; milestone and risk reports; beneficiary data; evaluations; completion or renewal decisions.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of effective sustainability partnerships with public and civil-society institutions. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Relationships are informal, philanthropic or lack defined objectives and results. 3 — Formal partnerships have relevant objectives, responsibilities and progress reporting. 4 — A portfolio of strategically aligned partnerships is governed against outcome indicators and produces documented institutional or beneficiary gains. 5 — Long-term co-created partnerships mobilise significant capability or capital, are independently evaluated and produce scalable system-level outcomes.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 8; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Strengthens technical capacity and sustainable finance programmes.

signals.signal: Joint sustainable-finance/green-finance initiatives
signals.definition: Co-financed or jointly delivered initiatives that mobilise additional capital for qualifying green, social or sustainability objectives and manage associated integrity risks.
signals.measurement: Track committed and deployed capital, qualifying uses, institution and partner contributions, private capital mobilised, beneficiaries or assets financed, additionality, safeguards, performance and impact outcomes.
signals.evidence_required: Facility or programme agreements; eligibility taxonomy; approvals; capital and disbursement records; leverage calculations; safeguards; portfolio and impact reports; independent evaluation; case studies.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of joint sustainable- or green-finance initiatives. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A memorandum or announced facility exists without deployed capital or verified eligible use. 3 — At least one governed initiative has defined eligibility and documented financing deployment. 4 — Multiple or material initiatives demonstrate additional capital mobilisation, safeguard compliance and measured financial and sustainability outcomes. 5 — Innovative, scalable structures mobilise significant third-party capital with independent impact verification, high integrity and successful replication.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 8; NGX disclosure guidance
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Shows practical collaboration with measurable outcomes.

signals.signal: Knowledge contribution through data sharing, joint products and client capacity building
signals.definition: Contribution to market capability through useful data, practical tools, jointly developed products and sustained capacity building for clients, peers or ecosystem participants.
signals.measurement: Assess usefulness and quality of contributions, audiences reached, adoption or reuse, products launched, client capability gain, feedback, data safeguards and documented changes in practice or market outcomes.
signals.evidence_required: Published datasets or insights; methodology and data controls; co-developed product papers; workshop materials; reach and adoption analytics; participant assessments; feedback; outcome or replication evidence.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of knowledge contribution through data, products and client capacity building. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Content or events are largely promotional and reach or adoption is not evaluated. 3 — Useful knowledge or training is periodically shared and participation or product uptake is tracked. 4 — Contributions are evidence-based, co-created where relevant and demonstrably adopted in client, peer or market practice. 5 — Open, high-quality knowledge assets and joint solutions achieve wide sustained adoption and verified sector-level capability or outcome gains.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principles 7 and 8; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Rewards active contribution rather than passive membership, but remains an enabling activity rather than a direct institutional outcome.

signals.signal: Regular sustainability/ESG reporting aligned with a recognised standard such as GRI or ISSB
signals.definition: Regular public disclosure of material sustainability information using a recognised reporting basis with a defined scope, reporting period and transparent index or compliance statement.
signals.measurement: Assess frequency and timeliness, entities and activities covered, stated reporting basis, content index, material-topic coverage, governance approval, comparatives, accessibility and alignment with applicable Nigerian adoption requirements.
signals.evidence_required: Published sustainability or annual report; reporting-basis statement; GRI content index or ISSB compliance statement; scope and boundary note; materiality assessment; governance approval; publication record.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of regular reporting aligned with a recognised sustainability standard. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Narrative sustainability information is published irregularly or without a defined reporting basis and boundary. 3 — A recurring report references a recognised standard and covers core material topics and performance. 4 — Annual reporting has clear boundaries, comparatives and a complete index or compliance statement and is subject to robust governance review. 5 — Reporting is fully aligned with applicable requirements, connected to financial reporting, digitally accessible and recognised for decision-useful transparency and continuous improvement.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 9; IFRS S1; FRC Nigeria adoption roadmap
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Standardised disclosure improves comparability between institutions and across reporting period and gives stakeholders visibility on sustainability performance.
