signals.signal: Quantitative disclosure of material ESG KPIs
signals.definition: Decision-useful quantitative disclosure of material environmental, social and governance performance indicators with consistent methods, boundaries, baselines and comparatives.
signals.measurement: Assess KPI coverage of material topics, units and definitions, entity and value-chain boundaries, baseline and prior-year comparatives, calculation methods, data controls, estimates, restatements and linkage to strategy.
signals.evidence_required: Published KPI tables; metric definitions; boundary and methodology notes; source-system extracts; reconciliations; control sign-offs; comparative and restatement schedules; governance review.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of quantitative disclosure of material ESG KPIs. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — A few standalone metrics are published without complete definitions, boundaries or comparatives. 3 — Core material KPIs have defined units and at least some baseline or comparative information. 4 — A comprehensive KPI set has consistent methods, boundaries, data controls and multi-period comparatives linked to material risks and targets. 5 — High-quality granular metrics are independently assured, digitally usable and demonstrably integrated with financial, strategic and risk analysis.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 9; IFRS S1 metrics and targets
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Allows performance to be assessed and compared.

signals.signal: Complete and timely NSBP/CBN regulatory returns
signals.definition: Complete, accurate and timely submission of required Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles returns and related CBN regulatory information.
signals.measurement: Track required returns, on-time submission rate, validation errors, resubmissions, data reconciliation, unresolved exceptions, supervisory feedback and management certification for each period.
signals.evidence_required: Regulatory calendar; completed returns; submission receipts; validation and reconciliation reports; sign-offs; correspondence; resubmission history; issue and remediation tracker.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of complete and timely NSBP and CBN regulatory returns. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Returns are late, incomplete, weakly controlled or cannot be reconciled to underlying data. 3 — Required returns are generally submitted with documented review, though some errors or delays occur. 4 — All returns are timely, complete, reconciled and certified, with exceptions promptly corrected and root causes addressed. 5 — A mature controlled reporting process has sustained error-free performance, automated validation and demonstrable readiness for supervisory review.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 9; CBN reporting template
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Shows compliance and formal monitoring of implementation.

signals.signal: Independent assurance/verification of ESG information
signals.definition: Independent assurance or verification that increases confidence in the accuracy, completeness and reliability of material sustainability information and underlying controls.
signals.measurement: Assess provider independence and competence, assurance standard and level, scope of topics and entities, materiality threshold, qualifications, findings, management response, publication and year-on-year scope growth.
signals.evidence_required: Signed assurance statement; provider credentials and independence; engagement letter and scope; assurance standard; findings and management letter; corrective actions; audit-committee review; public report.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of independent assurance of sustainability information. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Internal review or informal external checking occurs without a published independent conclusion. 3 — Independent limited assurance covers selected material KPIs and findings are addressed. 4 — Published assurance covers all material KPI categories and key reporting controls under a recognised standard with governance oversight. 5 — Broad, progressively stronger assurance covers connected narrative, metrics and controls with no material qualifications and demonstrable continuous improvement.
signals.primary_framework: GRI 2 external assurance; FRC Nigeria sustainability reporting guidance
signals.notes: Expanded analytical signal mapped to the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles. Final scores should be supported by direct signal-level evidence.
signals.justification: Improves reliability and credibility of reporting.

references.label: FRC Nigeria ISSB adoption roadmap and SRG 1 (2026)

signals.signal: Disclosure of progress against targets and material incidents
signals.definition: Balanced disclosure of progress against stated sustainability targets together with material incidents, missed targets, data changes and corrective actions.
signals.measurement: For each target, report baseline, deadline, current result, status and variance; track material incidents by type and severity, impacts, regulatory action, remedy, recurrence, restatements and action closure.
signals.evidence_required: Published target scorecard; baseline and result calculations; variance explanations; corrective plans; material-incident register; regulatory correspondence; remedy evidence; restatement log; board review.
signals.score_guide: 0 — No credible evidence of transparent target progress and material-incident disclosure. 1 — A commitment or isolated activity exists, but there is no approved, repeatable process. 2 — Only achievements are highlighted, while target status, adverse events or setbacks are omitted or vague. 3 — Progress against selected targets and significant incidents is reported with basic explanations. 4 — All material targets have comparable status and variance disclosure; incidents, remedies and corrective actions are reported under clear materiality rules. 5 — Candid, timely and independently assured disclosure explains trade-offs, restatements and outcomes and shows that lessons materially improve strategy, controls and accountability.
signals.primary_framework: CBN NSBP Principle 9; IFRS S1; GRI 2
